title: MOD takes sign of dividend; MODULO takes sign of divisor — differ on negative inputs
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE WRAP_INDEX(K, N, WRAPPED)
C     Bucket-index helper. MOD(-7, 5) = -2 (sign of dividend), but
C     MODULO(-7, 5) = 3 (sign of divisor). Java/C# % matches MOD,
C     Python's % matches MODULO. A naive port to (K % N) is wrong
C     for negative K when the legacy used MODULO -- and vice versa.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER K, N, WRAPPED
C     Source happens to use MOD here. The author MEANT MODULO; the
C     bug shipped to production for years.
      WRAPPED = MOD(K, N)
      IF (WRAPPED .LT. 0) WRAPPED = WRAPPED + N
      RETURN
      END
notes: The MOD-vs-MODULO trap surfaces in EVERY hash-bucket / cyclic-index pattern translated from Fortran. The 2-line adjustment after MOD (the IF WRAPPED.LT.0 line) is the legacy fix for negative inputs — the spec MUST capture this as an invariant or the rewrite drops a critical 2 lines that look like dead code to a reviewer.
